purpose: Full-size North American P-51D dimensions (metres) and the kit values that scale them. build_geometry.py turns this into geometry.json; nothing here is used by the app directly.

full_size.frame: z along the fuselage, positive aft, z = 0 at the wing leading edge on the centreline; y up, y = 0 on the propeller axis (thrust line); x to the right
full_size.stab_incidence_note: 0 deg assumed; Ziroli's 1/4.6 model uses stab +1 deg with wing +2.5 deg (decalage 1.5 deg)

section.name: NAA/NACA 45-100 (P-51D), UIUC ordinates: root BL17.5 (p51droot.dat), tip BL215 (p51dtip.dat)
section.camber: parabolic approximation y_c = 4 m x (1 - x), m = camber_ratio (UIUC root camber 1.26 % at 39 %, tip 1.30 % at 46 %)
section.source: https://m-selig.ae.illinois.edu/ads/coord/p51droot.dat and p51dtip.dat; local copies references/p51-mustang/airfoils/ (hashes in references/p51-mustang/index.json)

kit.name: P-51D Mustang 1/4 scale, 120 cc class (plans/short-kit class: Chad Veich 1/4 plans, Jerry Bates 1/4, FokkeRC 1/4 short kit)
kit.engine: Desert Aircraft DA-120 (121 cc twin, 11.7 hp, 2.45 kg with ignition) or DLE-120 class

propeller.note: DA-120 list: 2-blade 27x11/28x10/28x12, 3-blade 26x12/27x12; a 4-blade 26x12 is chosen for the scale look (estimated load)

kit.cg_note: Hangar 9 60cc: 171 mm behind the root LE (range 165-178) at 1/5 scale; CARF: front edge of the wing tube; Ziroli: 8-1/4 in behind the LE at the fuselage at 1/4.6. Converted to MAC with the LE extension these cluster at 25-30 % MAC; 27 % chosen (estimated)
kit.throws_note: Hangar 9 HAN4770 high rates (aileron 22 mm up, elevator 25 mm, rudder 55 mm) scaled by span 2.82/2.26 = 1.25; CARF (2.54 m) high rate: aileron 12.7 mm, elevator 19 mm up, rudder 51 mm

full_size.overall.source: P-51D: span 37 ft 0 in / 11.28 m, length 32 ft 3 in / 9.83 m (warbirdsresourcegroup.org, DCS manual p18); wing area 235 ft2 (WRG) / 233.19 ft2 (DCS); propeller 11 ft 2 in (DCS). URLs and hashes in docs/research/p51-resources.json
full_size.overall.limits: Fuselage sections, station lines, scoop and canopy proportions are read by eye from the public-domain AN 01-60-3 three-view (references/p51-mustang/drawings/), not measured on a calibrated plan. Gear track 11 ft 10 in and 27 in / 12.5 in wheels are unverified.

full_size.wing.source: plan-view silhouette fit: root chord 105.0 in (extrapolated to the centreline), tip 48.3 in, LE sweep 14.5 in at the tip; dihedral 5 deg and wing reference line 26.5 in below the FRL printed on the drawing

full_size.tail.source: Mason (Virginia Tech) P-51D configuration study: horizontal 45.4 ft2, span 13.1 ft, chords 4.6/2.3 ft; vertical 14.8 ft2, span 4.7 ft, chords 4.7/1.6 ft (references/p51-mustang/papers/)
full_size.tail.limits: Dorsal fillet and positions along the fuselage are read from the three-view.

section.source: UIUC p51droot.dat (BL17.5: t/c 16.5 % at 39 %, camber 1.26 %) and p51dtip.dat (BL215: 11.4 % at 46 %, camber 1.30 %)
section.limits: The builder uses the root thickness distribution with a parabolic camber line; the true camber line is not reproduced.

kit.source: No commercial ARF exists for 100-150 cc (research 2026-10-06): 1/4-scale plans (Veich: 284.5 cm, 1.36 m2, 18-27 kg; Bates 112 in, 50 lb+; FokkeRC 111 in, Kolm 155 cc). Engine DA-120 (desertaircraft.com, toni-clark.com). CG/throws from the Hangar 9 60cc, CARF and Ziroli manuals (references/p51-mustang/manuals/)
kit.limits: Exact 1/4 scale assumed; the propeller choice and the throws are estimates.

full_size.profile.source: research/p51/p51-02/silhouette/metrology.json: filled silhouettes of the AN 01-60-3 three-view (public domain), each axis calibrated with a printed dimension; applied by apply_metrology.py
full_size.profile.method: fuselage top/bottom from the side view, half-widths from the plan (interpolated under the wing and stab), canopy top line, scoop dip, spinner, wing/stab planforms (reserved checks: stab span +0.5 %, wing area +0.6 %, MAC +0.7 %)
full_size.profile.limits: the drawing's side view is ~3 % anisotropic (heights vs length); scoop and canopy widths are estimates; the wing root LE extension of the D is not modelled; fin and rudder lines are read from the top contour
